title: GPU Dispatcher Topology and Stability Protocol
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document defines the GPU Dispatcher Topology and Stability Protocol (GD-TSP) — a cross-cutting operational spec for how the serving runtime maps inference requests to GPU execution resources, how we validate topology changes with controlled benchmarking and profiling, and the runbooks to recover from topology-induced instability. It consolidates architecture intent, kernel scheduling implications, profiling playbook steps, benchmark protocols, release notes conventions for topology changes, and a curated list of known issues with pragmatic mitigations.

Intended audience:
- Runtime engineers responsible for dispatcher, scheduler, and kernel mapping
- SREs and oncall responders for inference fleet
- Performance engineers running micro/scale benchmarks
- Private deployment engineers planning topology configuration changes

Goals and invariants:
- Maintain tail-99 latency SLOs under mixed workloads (default SLO: 99th percentile <= 120ms for small-chat profile, see benchmark section).
- Keep graceful degradation semantics: requests should fallback to lower-cost model variants or queued/burst paths before hard rejecting.
- Ensure dispatcher topology changes are reversible and validated by automated benchmark and profiling gates.
- Provide an action-oriented runbook for common stability regressions caused by topology changes.

1) Topology primitives and terminology:
- GPU pool: a named group of homogeneous or compatible GPUs (e.g., g.pool.a100-80gb-q8).
- Dispatcher shard: logical unit inside the dispatcher mapped to a GPU pool shard (1:many mapping possible).
- Hotpath connector: low-latency path (no preemption) reserved for priority requests (priority class >= 100).
- Coldpath connector: higher-throughput, preemptible pool used for background or low-priority requests.
- Kernel affinity profile: a selected set of kernels (FP16/INT8/Triton fallback) and launch parameters pinned per GPU pool.
- KV-cache partitioning policy: descriptor for how KV caches are split across shards (range, hash, or LRU-slab).

2) Topology design guidelines (high level):
- Prefer narrower shards for high-priority low-latency workloads. Narrow shards = fewer concurrent requests per GPU; reduces queuing variance.
- Co-locate coldpath workloads on quantized kernels to save memory and throughput; avoid mixing with hotpath FP16 kernels on same physical GPU when latency SLOs are tight.
- Use NUMA-aware placement for on-prem racks: ensure dispatcher shards respect PCIe locality and do not cross NUMA domains for KV-heavy models.
- Configure dispatcher to expose a per-shard concurrency cap and a soft-threshold for admission (default soft-threshold = 0.75 * concurrency_cap).

3) Kernel scheduling implications and constraints:
- Kernel preemption cost: long-running fused kernels (e.g., long-sequence rotary attention fused kernels) increase preemption penalty. Documented rule: if average kernel_time > 12ms, prefer non-preemptive placement for hotpath.
- Continuous batching policy interacts with shard width. Wider shards yield larger effective batch sizes; use batch size caps to avoid OOM and increased p99.
- Kernel selection ramp: when upgrading kernels, ramp through alpha->canary->general with checkpointed perf baselines. Kernels must pass microbenchmarks for latency, tail, and throughput before rollout.

4) Profiling playbook for topology changes (step-by-step):
Pre-change checklist:
1. Record current topology manifest and active dispatcher routing table (CLI: redwoodctl dispatcher export --namespace <ns> --output json).
2. Capture baseline traces for 30 minutes using the standard sample policy (trace-level: request, kernel, and NVML counters).
3. Run the lightweight synthetic smoke test for correctness (single-turn, deterministic prompt).

Change-and-profile steps:
1. Apply topology change in a canary shard (apply to 1–3 GPUs) during low-traffic window.
2. Start continuous microbenchmark runner against canary for 60 minutes: 5 workload profiles (small-chat, assistant-long, embedding-batch, rerank, multimodal-lite).
3. Collect the following telemetry: per-request latency histograms, kernel latency distributions, GPU utilization, memory clocks, power draw, NVLink traffic, KV-cache hit ratios, and preemption counts.
4. Correlate sudden p99 jumps with kernel-time percentiles and preemption_count spikes.
5. If p99 delta > +20% or average GPU DRAM rising > 10% relative to baseline, automatically roll back.

Profiling artifacts to produce:
- Canary-report-YYYYMMDD.csv (rows: timestamp, workload, p50, p95, p99, qps, avg_gpu_mem_mb, kv_hit_ratio)
- Flamegraphs for kernel stacks (symbolized)
- NVML time-series segments clipped to incident window

5) Benchmark suite protocol (how we validate topology changes end-to-end):
Purpose: Provide reproducible, comparable results to gate dispatcher topology changes in CI and pre-prod.

Benchmark harness configuration (table):
- scenario: small-chat | assistant-long | embedding-batch | rerank | mixed-burst
- seq_len: 32 | 512 | 512 | 128 | variable
- concurrency: 200 | 40 | 16 | 80 | variable
- duration: 10m | 20m | 10m | 15m | 30m
- metrics: p50,p95,p99,tail-qps,token-cpu-ms,token-gpu-ms,cost-per-token

Run protocol (numbered):
1. Provision an isolated pre-prod cluster matching the target topology (exact GPU models, A/B IP ranges, same kernel libs).
2. Seed with representative KV-cache warmup traffic for 20 minutes.
3. Execute bench harness with the scenario matrix above. 5 replicates per scenario to reduce variance.
4. Aggregate metrics and run statistical significance test (paired t-test on p99 across replicates).
5. Approve topology change if: p99 delta <= +5% and cost-per-token delta <= +3% and no memory OOM observed.

6) Release notes conventions for topology/kernel changes:
- Title: [Dispatcher Topology] <short summary> (e.g., "[Dispatcher Topology] Split hotpath shards for chat-v2").
- Body must include: rationale, list of affected clusters, benchmark artifacts links, canary rollout schedule, rollback conditions, owner and oncall rota.
- Must attach: canary-report CSV, microbench baseline JSON, and profiler flamegraphs.

7) Runbooks (quick actions for common symptoms):
Symptom A: sudden p99 spike across a single shard- Quick triage:
1. Verify alert and scope (redwoodctl metrics query --expr 'p99_latency{shard="<shard>"}').
2. Fetch latest kernel latency histogram from tracing service.
3. If preemption_count increased > 10x, toggle preemption_policy=soft for affected shard and re-run microbench.
4. If GPU memory increased abnormally, temporarily shrink concurrency_cap by 25% and initiate KV-cache eviction.
5. If immediate mitigation fails, reassign traffic off shard to fallback pool (CLI: redwoodctl dispatcher reroute --from <shard> --to <fallback>) and open incident.

Symptom B: OOMs observed on mixed workloads after topology change- Quick triage:
1. Inspect kernel allocations in the last 10 failures (tracing id list).
2. If new kernel introduced (kernel_version mismatch), revert kernel on shard.
3. Reduce batch size caps and restart worker process for shard.
4. Escalate to runtime-core-owner if OOM persists after 2 restarts.

8) Known issues catalog (selection with mitigations):
- Issue: KV-cache slab fragmentation causing steady growth of memory usage on long-lived shards.
  - Symptom: slowly increasing GPU memory footprint (~1-2% per day) without workload change.
  - Mitigation: schedule periodic slab compaction (cron: /opt/redwood/bin/kv_compact --shard <s> --threshold 0.6).

- Issue: NVLink saturation when cross-rack shard affinity incorrectly configured.
  - Symptom: decreased throughput and increased kernel latency during multi-query KV-syncs.
  - Mitigation: pin shards to same-rack GPUs or throttle KV-sync frequency; add NVLink utilization alarms.

- Issue: Incompatible quantized kernel causing subtle token-level regressions (micro hallucinations).
  - Symptom: rare semantic drift in assistant-long scenarios after kernel swap.
  - Mitigation: run evaluation prompt-set (eval-suite: semantic-coherence-001) in canary and require zero false positives before general rollout.

9) Ownership, SLAs and metrics to monitor:
- Owners: dispatcher-service -> runtime-dispatcher-team; kernel library -> runtime-kernel-team; top-level oncall -> eng-sre-inference.
- Critical metrics (monitor every minute): p50_latency, p95_latency, p99_latency, qps, gpu_mem_used_mb, gpu_util_pct, preemption_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, tail_retries
- Alert thresholds (examples): p99_latency > 1.2x baseline for >5m -> P1; OOM count > 3 in 1m -> P1; preemption_count spike > 50% -> P2.

10) Post-incident and improvement actions:
- For any topology-induced P1 incident, produce an incident summary with: timeline, root cause, perf artifacts, remediation steps, and a 30/60/90 day mitigation plan.
- Quarterly: run chaos experiments that randomly permute shard-to-GPU mappings in pre-prod and validate benchmark suite resilience.

Appendix A — Useful commands and examples:
- Export current dispatch topology:
  redwoodctl dispatcher export --namespace prod-east-1 --output json > topology-prod-east-20260214.json

- Temporarily reduce concurrency cap on shard:
  redwoodctl shard update --shard s.chat.hotpath.3 --concurrency-cap 24 --soft-threshold 18

- Canary-run microbench (example):
  bench-runner --scenario small-chat --target https://canary.dispatcher.prod --concurrency 150 --duration 10m --out canary-small-chat.csv

- Sample shard manifest snippet (YAML textual example):
  ---
  shard_id: s.chat.hotpath.3
  gpu_pool: g.pool.a100-80gb-q8
  concurrency_cap: 32
  preemption_policy: hard
  kernel_profile: fp16_fused_v2
  kv_partition: hash:mod-1024

Appendix B — Release checklist for topology changes (quick):
1. Create a change PR with topology manifest and bench plan attached.
2. Run unit/integration tests locally and in CI.
3. Execute benchmark harness in pre-prod (5 replicates).
4. Upload canary reports and request approval from runtime-kernel-team and eng-sre.
5. Schedule canary rollout and monitor gating metrics for 60m.
6. Proceed to staged rollout if gates pass; otherwise revert and file RCA.
